1.
Heard Shri Sushil, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri Ambrish Shukla, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the State respondents.

2. Present petition has been filed seeking quashing of the recovery citation dated 15.10.2024.
3.
We find that in the present case the main order dated 30.07.2024 has not been challenged.
The only prayer by drawing attention to paragraph 16 to 17 of the writ petition that the petitioner is ready and willing to deposit the outstanding dues in easy installments.

sentences.text: 4. On perusal of order dated 30.07.2024, we find that the penalty was imposed under section 51 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

5. Although certified copy of the said order has been filed but the said order was not under challenge, however, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel submits that the petitioner may be granted two months time to deposit the entire dues.

6. Accordingly, present petition stands disposed of with the observations that in case the entire amount due is deposited within a period of two months from today in two equal installments, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner pursuant to said recovery citation 15.10.2024.
